description: For a learner working through second-language video or text a little above their level, keeping the material whole and putting helps (glossary, replay, first-language explanation, model answer after an attempt, hints before answers) one step away under the learner's control is expected to support comprehension and vocabulary at least as well as withholding or pushing the same helps; no claim here tests on-demand against pushed helps, and learner control in general averages near zero.
title: Keep the learner in control of the information flow with on-demand tools and supports

description: For a student with a disability, bringing supports into the general class and school life and moving the student to a separate setting only for a documented need the supported class cannot meet, decided case by case by a team and reviewed against data, is expected to give learning no worse than separate placement and fuller participation; one review of non-randomised studies finds no average difference between inclusive and segregated placement, and no claim tests the case-by-case decision itself.
title: Least Restrictive Environment
